name: Sorting Algorithms - Overview
definition: Algorithms that arrange elements in a specific order (ascending/descending).
formula: Compare and swap elements based on ordering criteria
examples: Merge sort: O(n log n), divide-and-conquer
Quick sort: O(n log n) average, O(n²) worst

name: Binary Search
definition: Efficient search algorithm for sorted arrays by repeatedly dividing search interval in half.
formula: T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1) → O(log n)
examples: Search in sorted array: O(log n)

name: Dynamic Programming
definition: Method solving complex problems by breaking into simpler overlapping subproblems, storing results.
formula: Memoization or tabulation; optimal substructure

name: Greedy Algorithms
definition: Make locally optimal choice at each step hoping to find global optimum.
formula: Choose best option at current stage

name: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
definition: Finds shortest path from source to all vertices in weighted graph with non-negative edges.
formula: Greedy approach: O(V²) or O(E log V) with priority queue

name: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
definition: Graph traversal visiting all neighbors before moving to next level.
formula: Use queue; O(V + E) time complexity

name: Depth-First Search (DFS)
definition: Graph traversal exploring as far as possible along each branch before backtracking.
formula: Use stack or recursion; O(V + E)

name: Merge Sort
definition: Divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that divides array, sorts halves, then merges.
formula: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) → O(n log n)

name: Quick Sort
definition: Divide-and-conquer sorting using pivot to partition array into smaller and larger elements.
formula: Average: O(n log n); Worst: O(n²); In-place

name: Hash Tables
definition: Data structure providing O(1) average-case access using hash function to map keys to indices.
formula: hash(key) → index; Handle collisions with chaining or open addressing
examples: Chaining: linked lists at each bucket

name: Binary Search Trees
definition: Tree where each node has at most two children; left < parent < right.
formula: Search, insert, delete: O(log n) average, O(n) worst
examples: Balanced BST (AVL, Red-Black): O(log n) worst

name: Heaps
definition: Complete binary tree satisfying heap property: parent ≥ children (max-heap) or parent ≤ children (min-heap).
formula: Insert, delete: O(log n); Find min/max: O(1)

name: Graphs - Representations
definition: Data structures for representing graphs: adjacency matrix, adjacency list.
formula: Matrix: O(V²) space, O(1) edge check; List: O(V+E) space, O(degree) edge check
examples: Social networks: vertices = people, edges = friendships

name: Tries (Prefix Trees)
definition: Tree structure for storing strings where each path represents a word/prefix.
formula: Search, insert: O(m) where m is string length

name: Big-O Notation
definition: Asymptotic upper bound on growth rate of function; worst-case complexity.
formula: f(n) = O(g(n)) if ∃c, n₀: f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for n ≥ n₀

name: Time vs Space Complexity
definition: Time: computational steps; Space: memory used by algorithm.
formula: Often trade-off between time and space
examples: Recursion: implicit space from call stack

name: P vs NP
definition: P: problems solvable in polynomial time; NP: verifiable in polynomial time; P=NP is open question.
formula: P ⊆ NP; P = NP?
examples: Sorting is in P: O(n log n)

name: NP-Completeness
definition: Hardest problems in NP; if any NP-complete problem has polynomial solution, then P=NP.
formula: Problem is NP-complete if: (1) in NP, (2) all NP problems reduce to it

name: Amortized Analysis
definition: Average performance over sequence of operations, accounting for expensive operations spread over many cheap ones.
formula: Total cost / number of operations

name: Recursion and Recurrence Relations
definition: Function calling itself; complexity expressed as recurrence relation.
formula: Master theorem: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)
examples: Binary search: T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1) → O(log n)
Merge sort: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) → O(n log n)
